item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Seeing as people are expressing an interest in actually writing this up as a musical, I'd like to point out that this would probably make an underwhelming musical and any attempt to write a musical based on this would probably be seriously hamstrung by following the song-list presented here.

It's far too long, with far too many songs, many of which serve absolutely no purpose (I mean, at one point Bright finishes a song, only to begin another song about exactly the same thing), which is the most obvious problem. Including instrumentals and reprises, it came to 33 numbers in total, which is going to end up being a bloated musical. Additionally, it's rather different from the 'normal' balance for a musical, as the second act is slightly longer than the first.

Additionally, most of the songs don't really have a discernible mood or emotional thrust - a lot of them just serve to move the plot along. All the songs that would set the scene go into setting up the Foundation concept without introducing any of the emotional and character-based facets of the story - I mean, Kondraki doesn't even get a character introduction, when such a song would practically write itself.

A lot of the titles would make for poor songs (most of them are pretty boring dialogue lines), and I doubt the sense in writing the main romance theme as having a refrain of 'Screw Professionalism'. None of these titles really conjure up anything in my head - I'd be happy for someone to prove me wrong, but, well, there's no real poetry (for want of a better word) in any of them.

That said, I think the majority of the plot presented here would make a relatively strong basis for a musical - just the way the various musical numbers are worked in, and the way the numbers flow together, are not very good from a storytelling point of view.

This article was not written so that someone could fill in the blanks to write a real musical and then perform it. It was written as a detailed, but frivolous wiki in-joke (not that there's anything wrong with that - note that I upvoted the article), and is written to maximise the number of in-jokes it can make, not to produce a good musical.

If I was writing a Foundation musical based on this, I would use the plot but seriously trim and revise, or completely abandon, the score. Right now, I wouldn't consider a musical written from this song-list to be performable. I'd probably cut the list of numbers down to about 60% of what it is now (merging a lot of consecutive numbers), add one or two songs that would be useful, cut the Able sub-plot, remove a few roles that are mostly there for name-checks, and probably change the titles of a lot of songs while retaining their general role and concept.
